I give up. I did not change `/work/putnam_2022_a5.lean`, so it still contains the `sorry`.

The statement needs two things, and I don't have a feasible route to either:

- **Lower bound (Alice can guarantee 290):** I would need an explicit strategy for Alice on arbitrary board states and a proof that it keeps at least 290 cells uncovered against every Bob reply. That means an invariant over all configurations of free segments on a 2022-cell board.
- **Upper bound (Alice cannot guarantee more than 290):** For an arbitrary strategy `s`, I would need to construct a Bob strategy and show the terminal board has at most 290 uncovered cells. This is the hard half of the actual Putnam argument, and it is a game-value computation rather than a short calculation.

Formalizing both halves in Lean 4 without the ability to iterate against Mathlib sources, and without `native_decide` for the finite analysis, is far beyond what I can reliably finish here.
